ideas.name: Unit 3 in one page and starting a small business

en.text: Gardening, dairy farming, animal fattening, poultry and beekeeping are self-employment opportunities. To start a small business: choose a useful product, a good location, know your resources, plan distribution and activities, set a fair price, and record income and costs. Profit is income minus cost, P = I − C.

screens.title: Unit summary
paras: In Ethiopia, agriculture creates many jobs.
Horticulture is one sector, not yet fully used.
Gardening, dairy, fattening, poultry and beekeeping are all ways to work for yourself.

screens.title: Ideas to start a micro or small business
table: Offer something useful; make sure there are buyers
Choose a place buyers can reach
Know your people, tools, land and cash
Know the production and marketing steps
Set a price that covers costs and gives profit
Record income (I) and costs (C); profit P = I − C

screens.title: Worked example: profit
steps: A poultry keeper sells eggs: income I = 3,000 birr.
Feed and other costs: C = 2,200 birr.
Income is greater than cost, so it is a profit.
If C were 3,400 birr: P = 3,000 − 3,400 = −400 birr. That is a loss.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Income minus cost: P = I − C.

screens.ask: Abebe sells honey for 5,000 birr. His costs are 3,500 birr. His profit is ___ birr.
screens.clue: Subtract the cost from the income.
